comment: The sources the shipped section data is compiled from, each pinned by checksum.
The two PyPI packages are public and installable, which is what makes their part of the
compilation reproducible: anyone can run compile_sections.py and get byte-identical output.
The workbook is a supplied file, vendored here for the same reason - so a reviewer can re-run
the compilation and diff rather than take several thousand numbers on trust.
None of these is an Autodesk product and none is redistributed wholesale; only the numbers
they publish are, converted into StructureGen's format and attributed per record.

sources.describes: Verbatim exports of primary published section tables: ArcelorMittal Orange Book (dimensions to EN 10365:2017, produced by SCI), the SCI Blue Book, and the AISC Shapes Database v16.0. Metric sheets are in millimetres, square centimetres and kilograms per metre.

sources.author: Paulo Cachim
sources.describes: European hot rolled I and H sections (IPE, HEA, HEB, HEM) and cold formed hollow sections (CHS, RHS, SHS), in centimetres and kilograms per metre.

sources.author: Evan Faler
sources.describes: A transcription of the AISC Shapes Database v16.0, in inches and pounds per foot.
